questions.prompt: The immediate trigger of World War I was
choices: the assassination of the German emperor, Wilhelm II, in Berlin
the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
the German invasion of Poland
the Russian Revolution
questions.explanation: The assassination in Sarajevo set off the July Crisis.
choiceExplanations: The German emperor was not assassinated.
The assassination in Sarajevo set off the July Crisis.
questions.distinguisher: The victim was the heir to Austria-Hungary's throne, not the German emperor.

questions.prompt: Militarism contributed to World War I by
choices: ending competition for colonies
encouraging arms races only in colonies outside of Europe
encouraging arms races and detailed war plans
reducing the size of European armies
questions.explanation: Arms races and rapid mobilization plans made war more likely.
choiceExplanations: Militarism did not end imperial competition.
The arms race centered on Europe.
Arms races and rapid mobilization plans made war more likely.
questions.distinguisher: The naval race between Germany and Britain took place in Europe.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best explains why Britain entered the war in 1914?
choices: Germany invaded neutral Belgium
Serbia invaded Britain
Russia attacked Britain's colonies
Germany invaded Britain's colony in Belgium
questions.explanation: The German invasion of Belgium brought Britain into the war.
choiceExplanations: The German invasion of Belgium brought Britain into the war.
questions.distinguisher: Belgium was a neutral country, not a British colony.

questions.prompt: Which claim about the causes of World War I is most defensible?
choices: Several interacting causes turned a crisis into a general war
The assassination alone caused the war
The war was caused mainly by the economic crisis of the Great Depression
Imperial rivalry alone caused the war
questions.explanation: Alliances, militarism, imperialism, and nationalism combined with the trigger.
choiceExplanations: Alliances, militarism, imperialism, and nationalism combined with the trigger.
The trigger alone does not explain a world war.
questions.distinguisher: Imperial rivalry mattered, but alongside alliances, militarism, and nationalism.

questions.prompt: Balkan nationalism before 1914 is best understood in the context of
choices: the Cold War
the growth of Ottoman power over the Balkan peoples
declining Ottoman power and Slavic nationalism
the rise of fascism in Italy
questions.explanation: As Ottoman control weakened, Serbs and other Slavs sought national states.
choiceExplanations: As Ottoman control weakened, Serbs and other Slavs sought national states.
questions.distinguisher: Ottoman power in the Balkans was shrinking, not growing.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, which alliance included Britain in 1914?
choices: Britain and the Ottoman Empire
France, Russia, and Britain
Germany, Austria-Hungary, and Britain
Britain, Italy, and Austria-Hungary
questions.explanation: The passage lists France, Russia, and Britain.
choiceExplanations: The passage lists France, Russia, and Britain.
Germany was on the other side.
Italy and Austria-Hungary were allied with Germany in 1914.
questions.distinguisher: Britain was allied with France and Russia, not Germany.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 7.2 key concept: the causes of World War I included imperialist expansion and competition, territorial and nationalist disputes, alliance systems, and militarism
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing long-term causes of World War I
stimulusBlocks.text:
By 1914, Europe's great powers had divided into two alliance systems: Germany and Austria-Hungary on one side, and France, Russia, and Britain on the other. Germany and Britain had raced to build battleships, and every great power kept large armies with detailed plans for rapid mobilization.

Imperial rivalries over colonies, and nationalism in the Balkans, where Serbs and other Slavic peoples wanted their own states, raised tensions further. Historians debate how much weight each cause deserves, but most agree that no single factor explains the war.

questions.prompt: The final sentence of the passage best supports which claim?
choices: The war had no causes in Europe
Historians agree imperialism alone caused the war
Historians see the war as having several causes
Historians agree on one cause of the war
questions.explanation: Historians debate weight but agree no single factor explains it.
choiceExplanations: Historians debate weight but agree no single factor explains it.
questions.distinguisher: The passage says no single factor explains the war.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, Germany invaded Belgium because
choices: its war plan called for defeating France quickly
Belgium had attacked Germany
Britain asked Germany to occupy Belgium
its war plan called for defeating Russia first, then France
questions.explanation: The plan required a quick victory over France through Belgium.
choiceExplanations: The plan required a quick victory over France through Belgium.
France was to be defeated first.
questions.distinguisher: The plan was to defeat France first, then turn to Russia.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 7.2 key concept: an assassination in the Balkans triggered a crisis that alliance systems turned into a general war
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing the July Crisis of 1914
stimulusBlocks.text:
On June 28, 1914, a Bosnian Serb nationalist assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand, heir to the throne of Austria-Hungary, in Sarajevo. With German support, Austria-Hungary sent Serbia an ultimatum and then declared war. Russia mobilized to protect Serbia.

Germany's war plan called for defeating France quickly before turning on Russia, so Germany declared war on Russia and France and invaded neutral Belgium. Britain then declared war on Germany. Within about a week, a regional crisis had become a war among the great powers.

questions.prompt: The passage best supports the claim that the war spread quickly because
choices: Serbia attacked every great power
the assassination took place in Paris
alliances and war plans drew in the great powers
all powers wanted to protect Austria-Hungary
questions.explanation: Commitments and plans brought in Russia, Germany, France, and Britain.
choiceExplanations: Commitments and plans brought in Russia, Germany, France, and Britain.
